accepted_edits.reason: the s46 rewrite answers the four findings of the review composed at 08:26Z: the s45 wait, the arm and ruff obligations, a behavioural writer test with a disabling control, and the narrower claim in place of mtime and inode

findings.reason: without the declared wait the node either rebuilds §45's index or blocks, and every one of its four checks names a symbol that does not exist at its base.
findings.text: s46 is declared `implementable` but its whole body repairs §45's review-store index, and none of that exists on the tree it would be built on: `plan-section-depends-on` carries no `s46` key at all — `"s46": ["the-monitor-reads-each-fact-once#s45"]` is missing — while `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6cd3459136 HEAD` fails and `reckon/crew/` on the primary tree defines none of `record_written`, `store_index_run_digest`, `reconcile_foreign_write`, `_entry_facts` or `tests/test_the_review_store_is_indexed_by_its_writers.py`, so a dispatcher may launch s46 first and its negative control ("at the base revision, the in-place rewrite leaves the digest unchanged") cannot run because there is no digest to leave unchanged

findings.reason: the section as written lets the node deliver one test run whose log the plan never places, which is exactly what the sibling sections' arm obligations exist to prevent.
findings.text: s46's done-when ends at its negative control and drops the three obligations its sibling sections each carry — "The test files importing the changed modules add no failure against base in matched arms run as an `all_debug` partition job …", "Each arm's log sits under the run directory, opens with its revision and literal command, and ends in `EXIT=`", and the ruff clause — so the node is asked for a head result only, with no arm pair and no stated log location, and its promotion has no durable evidence to read

findings.reason: the guard s46 adds to stop a bypass would pass on a bypass it cannot see, in the same shape as the assertion §46 quotes the earlier review as finding unfalsifiable.
findings.text: the first done-when item lists every call in `reckon/` that writes a file under a `review-records` directory "by parsing the source" and asserts each one reaches `record_written`, a call-graph claim a source parse cannot settle: a write whose directory is computed from a variable, or reached through a helper one frame away, is neither enumerated nor resolved, and the only stated control covers the second item, so nothing shows the enumerator would fail on a new bypass

findings.reason: the section closes the bypass only for the code paths it is given scope to edit, leaving a stated defect unfixed without saying so or reducing the claim.
findings.text: the Why's second finding is "an in-place write leaves the directory mtime unchanged, so the index never sees the rewrite", and its stated remedy pairs closing the in-`reckon/` bypasses with recording mtime and inode in every entry, but no endpoint consumes those fields: §45's readers "never list or stat the store on a read" and the store-directory mtime is the only reconcile probe, so the rewrite remains invisible while its gate asserts only that the fields are present

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the files, sections and commits s46 cites resolve, judged against the tree its work depends on: `reckon/crew/review_records.py`, `review.py` and `plan_review.py` are on the primary tree, the reviewed head 6cd3459136 resolves in the indexed run's branch (`reviewed_head_sha` on the stored record at `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261113T082959041438-the-review-store-is-indexed-by-its-writers/review-records/`), and `tests/test_the_review_store_is_indexed_by_its_writers.py` exists on that branch — its absence from the primary tree is the wiring defect below, not a dangling pointer.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the write-site enumerator in the enumerator item of s46's done-when can pass without ever showing it would catch a new bypass.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — s46's done-when drops the matched base arms, the arm-log path and the ruff clause that §43, §44 and §45 each carry, so no gate evidence lands on a durable path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — "Every review-record write moves the index" and the write paths `tests/test_every_review_record_write_moves_the_index.py` and `record_written`/`mtime_ns`/`store_index_run_digest` name the mechanism, with no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s46 requires each index entry to carry the record's mtime and inode while every read path it and §45 define is forbidden to stat a record, so the added fields have no consumer and the in-place rewrite the Why describes as invisible from outside the writer path stays invisible.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s46 carries one deliverable, that the review store's index is the sole record of what the store holds, with the mtime/inode entry shape and the docstring as parts of the same claim.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — s46 repairs §45's index yet declares no `depends-on` on s45 and is marked implementable while every symbol it names exists only on §45's unlanded branch.
